text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Namibia's power crisis is now so serious that on some days the national power utility, Nampower, has to import 100 percent of Namibia's electricity from South Africa, according to Nampower managing director Leake Hangala.
- Petrol and diesel prices fall by five cents a litre from Wednesday.
- The Namibia Institute for Democracy and the directorate of elections is conducting a seminar for election assistants.
- President Sam Nujoma inaugurated a new craft and trade market in Otjiwarongo on Tuesday.
- Petrol and diesel prices dropped by five cents a litre at midnight on Tuesday.
- Parliamentary debate over the last few days over the increase in rape cases ended with high expectations for action on the part of the judiciary.
